answer: The water master counts every skin at each well and writes the tally in the caravan book, and the merchant checks the count against the skins he loaded at the bridge of the journey. A timber skin that was never counted is no skin at all: the count must match the well's own register, and a skin filled in secret holds no water. Faking a tally means bribing the water master, forging 300 counts and paying 12,600, while the summit mark burned into each skin is read at every oasis, so a skin whose tally was never written is emptied on the sand.
